Linux Boot Process: From Power Button to Login

Ever wondered what actually happens between pressing the power button and getting to your Linux login screen? Here’s a simple breakdown of what’s happening behind the scenes.

⚡ Power On
The computer receives power and starts the hardware needed to begin the boot process.

🧩 BIOS/UEFI
BIOS or UEFI is firmware built into the computer that runs before the operating system. It checks that essential hardware such as the CPU, RAM and storage is available, then looks for something it can boot from.

🔍 Hardware Detection
The system identifies the connected hardware and prepares it so the operating system can use it.

💾 Boot Device
BIOS/UEFI checks the configured boot order and finds the device containing the Linux installation, usually an SSD or hard drive.

🚀 GRUB Bootloader
GRUB is a bootloader commonly used by Linux. It loads the Linux kernel and can also give you options to select a different kernel or operating system.

🐧 Linux Kernel
The kernel is the core of Linux. It takes control of the hardware, manages resources such as CPU and memory, and starts the processes needed to bring the system up.

⚙️ systemd
Once the kernel is running, systemd becomes the first process in user space. It starts and manages the services required by the system.

🔧 Targets and Services
systemd works through targets and starts services such as networking, SSH and other processes needed to bring the system into an operational state.

🔐 Login
Once the required services are running, the login screen or terminal prompt becomes available and you can start using the system.

Once you understand what each stage is doing, the Linux boot process becomes much easier to follow.

Vous utilisez Claude comme un simple chatbot ? Vous passez probablement à côté de son véritable potentiel.

Un dirigeant commercial chez Anthropic a partagé 3 façons d'utiliser Claude Cowork avec son équipe. Ces automatisations peuvent vous faire gagner plusieurs heures chaque semaine.

1. Préparer automatiquement vos appels
Chaque matin, Claude récupère les informations utiles : dépenses, état du pipeline dans Salesforce, données internes et réunions prévues dans l'agenda. Résultat : un briefing synthétique est généré pour chaque rendez-vous avant même le début de la journée.

2. Mettre vos prévisions hebdomadaires en pilote automatique
Chaque vendredi, Claude rassemble les opportunités en cours, les prévisions commerciales et les notes internes, puis génère un rapport prêt à être partagé avec toute l'équipe avant la réunion. Une tâche chronophage transformée en automatisation récurrente.

3. Faire avancer vos projets stratégiques pendant la nuit
Pour prioriser ses comptes clients, une équipe a demandé à Claude d'analyser plus de 4000 comptes à partir d'une grille de notation. Le lendemain matin, chaque compte disposait d'un score, d'une justification détaillée et des données associées. Claude a même généré un tableau de bord interactif pour repérer instantanément les comptes les plus prometteurs.

La vraie question n'est plus "que pouvez-vous demander à Claude ?", mais "quelles tâches pouvez-vous arrêter de faire manuellement dès cette semaine ?"

          How to Fake a LinkedIn Post, A Short Guide.
          Firstly, start with a claim that no one can verify. "Last week, I spoke with 12 hiring managers..." no you didn't, Steven.
          Next, pick a number that SOUNDS like it might be real. 12 sounds good. Maybe.
          Stick a disclaimer in for the next bit. "I almost didn't post this..." because ov course you "almost didn't."
          Make a summary of what you "learned," as if this wasn't a completely made up scenario in your head. Astounding work.
          Don't forget to throw in a fake quote that no real human being would ever say, like, "We’re really just looking for someone who can take ownership."
          Don't ever mention specifics because then people can hold you accountable. Be as vague as you possible can to get away with it.
          End with a soft CTA so people will message you!
          If this is what passes for #content for you, then you should probably get off LinkedIn and touch grass. It's 2026. Let's leave ChatGPT writing our LinkedIn updates wholesale and coming up with spurious numbers no one can verify back in 2025. You're better than that. Stop lying to people.

          Last month, I completed my six years of service as a member of the Board of Directors for Girl Scouts of New Mexico Trails. When I submitted my application in the fall of 2019, I could not have foreseen everything that lay ahead; none of us could. But I will now confess that I was woefully underinformed about serving on a Board (my fault entirely).

          “I love the Girl Scouts,” I thought. “I’m a proud Girl Scout Alum. This will be like being a Brand Ambassador with a side of fundraising.”

          Wrong. I was wrong. At best, this is a very incomplete understanding of serving on the governing board of a nonprofit organization.

          𝗪𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝗜‌ 𝗹𝗲𝗮𝗿𝗻𝗲𝗱: 𝗳𝗶𝗱𝘂𝗰𝗶𝗮𝗿𝘆 𝗿𝗲𝘀𝗽𝗼𝗻𝘀𝗶𝗯𝗶𝗹𝗶𝘁𝘆 𝗶𝘀𝗻'𝘁 𝗮𝗯𝘀𝘁𝗿𝗮𝗰𝘁​ — 𝗶𝘁'𝘀 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝘄𝗲𝗶𝗴𝗵𝘁 𝗼𝗳 𝗺𝗮𝗸𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗱𝗲𝗰𝗶𝘀𝗶𝗼𝗻𝘀 𝘁𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝗮𝗳𝗳𝗲𝗰𝘁 𝗽𝗲𝗼𝗽𝗹𝗲 𝘆𝗼𝘂'𝗹𝗹 𝗻𝗲𝘃𝗲𝗿 𝗺𝗲𝗲𝘁. It's understanding that every financial decision either expands or limits opportunities for girls across New Mexico. When you're deliberating and voting, you're not thinking about this quarter. You're thinking about whether Girl Scouts will still be here, still be strong, still be serving girls in 2030, 2040, 2050.

          The hardest part is being a voice for people who aren't in the room. When board conversations happen, the girls we serve aren't there. Volunteers in rural communities three hours from Albuquerque aren't there. Families who can’t afford transportation to events aren’t there. Like most organizations, we hear most from the people already engaged​ — the troop leaders who come to trainings, the parents who respond to surveys, the members who show up for Annual Meetings.

          But the Girl Scout Law reminds us to "be a sister to 𝘦𝘷𝘦𝘳𝘺 Girl Scout." Someone has to ask: "How does this decision affect the girls we're not hearing from? What are we missing from our perspective?" The responsibility to actively imagine and advocate for people beyond your own experience felt like a culmination of my personal values and my professional skills.

          I learned so much serving under two CEOs: Rebecca Latham and @Celia Tellez. They showed me what it looks like to balance the immediate needs of the organization with the long-term mission. To make hard calls with limited resources. To keep showing up for girls even when everything felt impossible, ahem, global pandemic, ahem.

          Would I do it again? Absolutely. But I'd go into it knowing: board service isn't cheerleading. It's stewardship. It's sitting with difficult questions and accepting that perfect answers don't exist. It's doing the unsexy work of governance because you believe the mission matters more than your comfort.

          Photo: Me and my friend Erin Barrio. Erin began her term on the Board the same day my tenure ended. Erin is also a former Girl Scout, so of course she showed up energized, prepared, and ready to work.

          11mo • Edited

          After 4 decades in legal tech, from working in law firms to now developing solutions for them, I say with certainty:

          The culture you build determines the future you create.

          2000s: Building nQ Zebraworks from a startup into a company serving the largest law firms in the world meant redefining what "dedication" looked like. Red-eye flights became routine, never flying during daylight hours because that was "wasted" work time. I'd even purposefully work from the UK or AU during American holidays, thinking I was being efficient by gaining an extra day. All-nighters to meet client deadlines weren't occasional; they were expected. Vacations? Planned, paid for, and then canceled at the last minute because a client needed us. Or worse yet, my family would go on the vacation without me because I chose work.

          I told myself this was what it took to build something meaningful. That sacrificing sleep, health, and time with family was the price of success. I watched my team do the same, and I was proud of our commitment.

          But I was wrong.

          2010s: As nQ grew into a global company, something shifted. I started losing good people, not to competitors, but to burnout. Talented team members who could have thrived for decades left because they couldn't sustain the pace. I saw the costs mounting: health issues, broken relationships, creativity that dried up from exhaustion.

          The irony? Our clients, those prestigious law firms, were starting to ask their own questions about associate retention and mental health. And here we were, perpetuating the same unsustainable culture we were supposed to be helping them solve.

          I realized that the culture I'd built was replicating the worst parts of what I'd experienced in the 80s and 90s. I was passing down a legacy of exhaustion, not excellence. Looking back now with 30+ years of perspective, I realize we had it backwards.

          Here's what I've learned: The best solutions come from people who have space to think, not from those who stayed latest. Real breakthroughs happen when teams have energy to ask "what if?" instead of just "what's next?"
          Now, I build teams differently. I look for people who know when to push hard and when to step back. Who measure impact by problems solved, not hours logged.

          The results? Higher retention. Stronger innovation. We're still landing the biggest clients in legal tech, but with teams that aren't running on fumes.

          I bike more. I'm present for family dinners (and vacations!). My team sees that balance isn't just lip service, it's modeled from the top.

          The truth is simple: You can't build a sustainable company on unsustainable practices. The culture you create today doesn't just affect your bottom line, it affects the lives of everyone who shows up to do the work. That's leadership.

          As we head into the holidays, I'm grateful for every mistake that taught me this lesson. And I'm committed to helping the next generation of legal tech leaders.

          #LegalTech #WorkCulture #Leadership #WorkLifeBalance

                                  Don’t Worry. Bring It to God 🙏

                                  “Do not be anxious about anything, but in every situation, by prayer and petition, with thanksgiving, present your requests to God.” Philippians 4:6

                                  Worry drains your strength.
                                  Anxiety clouds your vision.

                                  But prayer?

                                  Prayer shifts your focus from the problem to the Provider.

                                  God never asks us to deny our struggles but He does invite us to bring them to Him.

                                  In every situation. Big or small. He listens.

                                  When we choose prayer over panic, we create space for His peace to fill what fear once occupied.

                                  The very next verse says: “And the peace of God, which transcends all understanding, will guard your hearts and your minds in Christ Jesus.” Philippians 4:7

                                  That’s the promise.

                                  Peace that's anchored in the One who never changes.

                                  Action Points: Turning Worry into Worship

                                  • Pause and pray before you panic. Don’t let anxiety take the lead. Prayer realigns your heart.

                                  • Make a list of your worries and surrender them one by one. Write down what’s weighing on you, and pray over each one.

                                  • Add thanksgiving to your prayers. Gratitude shifts your focus and strengthens your trust.“Lord, I thank You for what You’ve already done and what You’re going to do.”

                                  • Memorize Philippians 4:6–7. Speak it out loud when worry tries to take over.

                                  • Tell someone you trust. Invite a fellow believer to pray with you and walk with you.

                                  A Prayer Based on Philippians 4:6
                                  Father, You know what’s weighing on me. You see every burden, every question, every quiet fear. Today, I choose to bring it all to You, in prayer and with thanksgiving. Thank You that You are near and that You care. Replace my anxiety with Your peace, and guard my heart and mind in Christ Jesus. I trust You. I surrender it all. In Jesus’ name, amen.

                                  She saved it.”

                                  But Elijah just smiled and whispered in her ear:

                                      After 36 years of running through airports and barely making security lines while perfecting my "conference handshake-to-coffee ratio," the numbers are in: I have flown over 146,000 miles ✈️ attending International Legal Technology Association (ILTA) 36 times over the past 40+ years. I wonder if they still offer those unlimited flights for life passes? Stayed for 150+ hotel nights PLUS breakfasts. I know which hotels have the best breakfasts 🥞. Shaken over 7,000 different hands. I don’t know if I need hand-sanitizer at this point or if the germs have just recycled. And met over 3,000 individual companies 🏢.

                                      But here's the thing – behind all those frequent flyer miles and "Do Not Disturb" hotel door hangers is ONE simple mission: building software that doesn't make lawyers want to throw their laptops out the window.

                                      As CEO of Scan Logic and a legal tech veteran who's seen it all, including floppy disks and fax machines, my purpose remains unchanged: developing powerful, intuitive solutions that actually solve real problems for legal professionals.

                                      Because after 36 ILTACONs, countless conversations, and enough airport coffee to fuel a small law firm, I've learned that great legal technology isn't about the bells and whistles – it's about making connections and lawyers' lives easier so they can focus on what matters most, their clients.

                                      Here's to ILTACON next week and whatever airline status tier comes after "We're basically family at this point."

                                      How many ILTACONs have you attended? I would love to see how many old friends are celebrating 36 this year too! See you there! Visit us at booth #529

                                                      🧠 Lors de mon intervention aux Arts et Métiers - École Nationale Supérieure d'Arts et Métiers pour le module APE, un sujet revenait souvent chez les élèves :
                                                      « Comment je fais pour me vendre sans me survendre ? »
                                                      « Comment éviter de passer pour quelqu’un d’arrogant ou d’effacé en entretien ? »

                                                      🎯 Ma réponse : ne pas se vendre, mais donner envie d’acheter.

                                                      Et pour ça, il faut comprendre l’intention derrière chaque mot, et savoir créer de l’impact sans forcer.

                                                      Ce que je leur ai transmis :
                                                      🔸 Le pouvoir de l’objectif clair, posé dès le départ
                                                      🔸 Les techniques de suggestion indirecte (nos fameux “sujets de paille” 😉)
                                                      🔸 La posture de celui ou celle qui mène l’entretien, plutôt que de le subir
                                                      🔸 Des outils issus du coaching, testés dans des contextes très concrets (entretiens, rendez-vous pro, réseaux)

                                                      Et ils ont compris
                                                      Ils ont intégré
                                                      Et surtout… ils ont appliqué

                                                      💡 Le plus puissant dans tout ça ?
                                                      Ce sont des compétences humaines qui serviront toute leur carrière, bien au-delà de la recherche de stage.

                                                      🔥 L’enseignement supérieur évolue !

                                                      Il ne s’agit plus seulement d’apprendre des formules, mais aussi de se comprendre soi, pour mieux se positionner face aux autres.

                                                      Et ça, c’est un vrai progrès.

                                                      💬 Et vous, quelles techniques relationnelles ont changé votre manière de réussir vos entretiens ou vos rendez-vous ?

                                                      ✔️ la communication authentique et efficace

                                                      Et c’est exactement pour ça que je fais ce métier.

                                                      Encore merci Maureen pour la confiance que tu m'as accordée 🙏

                                                      ➡️ Vous sentez cet écart entre ce que vous vivez… et ce que vous voulez vraiment ?

                                                      Je suis là pour en parler.
                                                      #coaching #transitionpro #alignement #sens #déclic

                                                      Maureen VASSEUR

                                                      • 2nd

                                                      Experte en communication & stratégie digitale 👩‍💻 | J’aide les TPE/PME à clarifier leur message et devenir visibles

                                                      1yr

                                                      🔁 Ce que je m’apprête à publier ici, je ne pensais pas le faire un jour.
                                                      Pendant plusieurs mois, j’ai gardé ce projet pour moi. 𝗝'𝗮𝗶 𝘁𝗿𝗮𝘃𝗮𝗶𝗹𝗹𝗲́ 𝗲𝗻 𝘀𝗶𝗹𝗲𝗻𝗰𝗲.

                                                      Peu de gens étaient au courant. Parce que j’avais besoin d’un espace rien qu’à moi, d’un moment "hors cadre" pour faire le point, me recentrer, et prendre du recul sur ma vie pro.

                                                      J’ai été accompagnée dans cette démarche par                                                       Sylvain HOAREAU, un coach professionnel aussi bienveillant que précis, aussi humain que structurant.

                                                      Il m’a permis de poser des mots justes, de regarder mon parcours autrement, et de redessiner ma trajectoire à partir de ce que je suis (vraiment).

                                                      🧭 Je ressentais le besoin de comprendre ce qui me fait vibrer, ce que je veux vraiment. Ce qui me correspond profondément. Ce qui me nourrit, et ce qui me fatigue aussi.
                                                      J’ai eu envie de m’écouter. De me réaligner.

                                                      Ce travail m’a permis de revenir à l’essentiel. De mieux me connaître. Et d’assumer une décision importante.

                                                      ✨ Ce bilan a mis en lumière plusieurs choses :
                                                      • mon besoin d’𝗮𝗹𝗶𝗴𝗻𝗲𝗺𝗲𝗻𝘁, d’𝗶𝗺𝗽𝗮𝗰𝘁 𝗵𝘂𝗺𝗮𝗶𝗻 et de 𝘁𝗿𝗮𝗻𝘀𝗺𝗶𝘀𝘀𝗶𝗼𝗻
                                                      • mon envie d’être entourée de 𝗽𝗲𝗿𝘀𝗼𝗻𝗻𝗲𝘀 𝗾𝘂𝗶 𝗺’𝗶𝗻𝘀𝗽𝗶𝗿𝗲𝗻𝘁, 𝗾𝘂𝗶 𝗼𝗻𝘁 𝘂𝗻𝗲 𝘃𝗶𝘀𝗶𝗼𝗻, 𝗲𝘁 𝗮𝘃𝗲𝗰 𝗾𝘂𝗶 𝗷𝗲 𝗽𝗲𝘂𝘅 𝗰𝗼𝗻𝘀𝘁𝗿𝘂𝗶𝗿𝗲
                                                      • ma soif d’𝗮𝘂𝘁𝗼𝗻𝗼𝗺𝗶𝗲, de 𝘀𝗲𝗻𝘀, et de 𝗹𝗶𝗲𝗻 𝘃𝗿𝗮𝗶
                                                      • ma capacité à 𝗰𝗿𝗲́𝗲𝗿, 𝗶𝗻𝘀𝗽𝗶𝗿𝗲𝗿, 𝗿𝗲𝗯𝗼𝗻𝗱𝗶𝗿, même dans les périodes de flou

                                                      🌱 Je partage ce moment ici car je crois profondément en ce type d’accompagnement.
                                                      On n’a pas toujours les réponses seul.e.
                                                      Et parfois… on prend des décisions qu’on n’aurait pas osé faire sans ce cadre, cette écoute, ce miroir.

                                                      💥 J’ai donc pris une première décision forte : 𝗷’𝗮𝗶 𝗱𝗲́𝗺𝗶𝘀𝘀𝗶𝗼𝗻𝗻𝗲́.
                                                      Pas sur un coup de tête, vous l'aurez compris. Mais parce que ma vision a évolué, et qu’il était temps que mes choix la reflètent.

                                                      Je sais ce que je veux cultiver : 𝗱𝘂 𝘀𝗲𝗻𝘀, 𝗱𝘂 𝗹𝗶𝗲𝗻, 𝗱𝘂 𝗿𝗲𝘀𝗽𝗲𝗰𝘁, 𝗱𝗲 𝗹𝗮 𝗹𝗶𝗯𝗲𝗿𝘁𝗲́.
                                                      Et surtout, je me sens 𝗮̀ 𝗺𝗮 𝗽𝗹𝗮𝗰𝗲 dans ce nouveau chapitre qui s’ouvre.

                                                      Merci à tous ceux qui, sans le savoir, m’ont inspirée pendant cette étape.
                                                      Merci à moi aussi, d’avoir pris le temps.

                                                      Et si vous ressentez ce tiraillement, cette envie de changement, ce besoin d’alignement… faites-le.
                                                      Prenez ce temps pour vous.
                                                      Je ne peux que recommander cette démarche - et Sylvain, bien évidemment - 👌

                                                      À suivre ✨

                                                              1yr

                                                              When someone has a gap in their resume, I don’t ask why first.

                                                              I ask: What did you learn? What did it teach you about yourself?

                                                              Some of the most capable, grounded, and driven people I’ve worked with had gaps—because they were caretaking, healing, parenting, or starting over.
                                                              They’ve built things. Fought through things. Grown in ways a job title could never reflect.

                                                              So no—I don’t judge gaps.
                                                              Because I’ve had gaps of my own, too.
